instructions: Add Martin's shortlist records here. Use exhibitorId values from data/exhibitors.json.

selections.reason: Demo only: evaluate whether automation could reduce manual timber stacking and improve pack consistency.
questions: What timber sizes and weights can the system handle?
Can it work with variable-length hardwood packs?
What is the smallest practical installation footprint?
selections.notes: Replace this with real notes once a confirmed exhibitor is added.

selections.reason: Compare lower-cost Chinese translation earbuds and devices with Pete's Timekettle during Phase 1.
questions: Does English-Mandarin translation work fully offline?
Must the earbuds stay connected to a phone by Bluetooth?
Can two people each wear one earbud for a natural conversation?
Does the iPhone app and translation service work reliably in mainland China?
Can we buy a sample at the fair, and what is the retail or sample price?
How does the translation speed and accuracy compare with Timekettle?
selections.notes: Phase 1 target. Hall, booth and confirmed exhibitors still to be researched.

selections.reason: Motion and actuator supplier worth checking for compact linear movement, servo positioning and actuator technology that could form part of custom board handling, gripper positioning or transfer-table mechanisms.
questions: What payload and stroke ranges are available for the micro linear actuator range?
Can actuators be synchronised across multiple axes for long-object handling?
Do they supply controllers, APIs or PLC integration examples?
Can they customise actuator speed, duty cycle, sealing or mounting for dusty timber environments?
selections.notes: Official booth-confirmed lead. Not a complete timber stacker, but potentially useful motion hardware.

selections.reason: PLC, HMI, servo drive and VFD supplier; useful for the control layer of a timber stacking cell, conveyors, lift tables or briquette support equipment.
questions: Can their PLCs coordinate multiple servo axes for long timber handling?
Do they support common industrial protocols for robot, vision and conveyor integration?
What local or remote support is available for custom machine builders?
Can they show examples of packaging, stacking or material-handling machines using their controls?
selections.notes: Strong automation-controls stop in Area D before looking at physical handling equipment.

selections.reason: Drive and industrial automation supplier with booths in the Industrial Automation area and General Machinery area; useful for motor/VFD/control discussions for conveyors, transfer tables and production-line drives.
questions: Which drives suit dusty sawmill conveyors and lift tables?
Can their VFDs handle synchronized conveyor sections or positioning applications?
Do they have application examples in timber, packaging, palletizing or heavy material handling?
What PLC or API integration options are available?
selections.notes: Verify exact stand on the official Canton Fair app before travel because this lead came from SAJ's company social post.

selections.reason: Industrial automation and drive supplier; useful for VFD, motion-control and energy-efficiency questions around conveyors, motors, dust extraction and machinery upgrades.
questions: Which VFDs are recommended for conveyors, augers, fans and dust extraction?
Do they support multi-motor synchronisation or motion-control applications?
Can they provide examples for packaging, materials handling or wood-processing lines?
What support is available for Australian installations?
selections.notes: Not a timber-stacking supplier, but a useful electrical and drive-control stop if route time allows.

selections.reason: Material handling manufacturer with stackers, pallet trucks, forklifts and lift platforms. Not a timber stacking automation supplier, but very relevant for handling packs, movement between stations and practical load-handling hardware.
questions: What lifting capacities and fork lengths are available for long or uneven timber packs?
Can stackers or lift platforms be customised for long hardwood boards?
Do they offer attachments or fixtures for timber packs?
What spare parts and service support can they provide for Australia?
selections.notes: Verified version of the earlier external Niuli lead.

selections.reason: Very relevant to wood-waste and briquette-adjacent production: presswood pallet, block pallet, wood nailing and plastic extrusion equipment. Also mentions shredding/grinding and drying in related company material.
questions: Can their presswood process use Australian hardwood sawdust or mixed hardwood residues?
What particle size, moisture content and binder system are required?
Do they supply shredders, grinders, dryers, hoppers and conveyors as a complete line?
Can equipment be adapted from pallet blocks to briquettes or fuel blocks?
selections.notes: One of the best briquette/wood-residue leads found in this pass. Booth source is a company LinkedIn post, so cross-check in Canton Fair app.

selections.reason: Laser cutting is not core timber stacking, but may be useful for fabricating brackets, machine frames or custom metal parts for automation projects.
questions: Can their machines cut heavy tube or profiles for machine frames?
What support and spare parts are available internationally?
Do they provide nesting/software workflows suitable for custom fabrication?
selections.notes: Route filler in Hall 20.1 if already nearby for automation booths.

selections.reason: Packaging and production-line supplier with palletizing-machine capability; not timber-specific, but worth asking about adapting end-of-line automation concepts to briquette bagging, weighing, packing and palletising.
questions: Do they build palletizing cells or integrate third-party robots?
Can their conveyors, weighing or packing systems handle briquettes or wood-fuel products?
Do they supply complete lines with PLC integration and safety guarding?
Can they show examples outside beverage filling?
selections.notes: Best treated as a packaging/palletising lead, not a timber handling specialist.

selections.reason: Biomass boiler supplier relevant to briquette production economics and possible use of wood residue fuel; useful for understanding combustion, drying heat and steam/hot-water options.
questions: Can their biomass boilers run on hardwood briquettes or sawdust-derived fuel?
What fuel moisture and particle-size limits apply?
Can they provide heat for dryers in a briquette production line?
What emissions controls and certifications would be needed for Australia?
selections.notes: Supporting briquette-production equipment rather than briquette press machinery.

selections.reason: Strong timber-stacking-cell component lead: positioning sensors, safety light curtains and photoelectric sensing are relevant to pack detection, machine guarding, alignment and conveyor/robot cell safety.
questions: Which sensor technologies work reliably with dusty hardwood, variable surfaces and changing ambient light?
Can they recommend a sensor layout for detecting board/pack position and height on a conveyor?
What safety light-curtain options suit access guarding around a timber stacking cell?
Do their sensors support standard PLC and industrial-fieldbus connections?
selections.notes: Excellent technical stop in the Industrial Automation hall. This is component technology, not a complete robot cell. Confirm the stand in the official Canton Fair app before travel.

selections.reason: Useful material-handling benchmark for moving finished timber packs and comparing electric pallet stackers or reach-truck options around an automated cell.
questions: Which machines and attachments are suitable for long, uneven or heavy timber packs?
What lift capacities, fork lengths and aisle widths are achievable?
Can they supply custom forks, clamps or other timber-pack attachments?
What Australian support, spares and compliance documentation are available?
selections.notes: A supporting handling stop, not the automated stacking mechanism itself. It sits in the same Area D Hall 20.1 research cluster.

selections.reason: A practical alternative to a robot for moving long hardwood packs: overhead or mobile gantry-crane systems can span a production line and handle awkward loads where fork or robot reach becomes limiting.
questions: Can a gantry or overhead system lift long, uneven hardwood packs safely without board damage?
Do they design lifting beams, spreader bars or custom timber-pack fixtures?
What load-positioning accuracy and anti-sway options are available?
Can a crane be integrated with conveyors, sensors or semi-automated stacking stations?
selections.notes: One of the better real-world timber-pack handling leads. It is a crane/hoist solution, not an industrial robot arm.

selections.reason: Crane, gantry and lifting-beam supplier in the Industrial Automation hall. Relevant for assessing an overhead pack-handling mechanism or a semi-automated timber stacking station.
questions: Can they engineer a lifting beam or clamp arrangement for hardwood packs of varying lengths?
What options provide controlled, repeatable placement onto stacking bunks?
Can the crane be automated or interfaced with PLCs, positioning sensors and safety systems?
What Australian installation, certification and spares support is available?
selections.notes: High-value Hall 20.1 visit because it can be considered alongside sensors, controls and other automation-cell components.

selections.reason: AGV and AMR drive specialist. Useful for understanding whether automated mobile handling could move packs or pallets between sawmill process steps and a future stacking cell.
questions: What payload, gradient and floor-condition limits apply to their AGV/AMR drive solutions?
Can the drive technology be integrated into a custom long-load timber carrier?
What safety sensing and fleet-control interfaces are supported?
Do they have examples of heavy, dusty industrial applications rather than clean warehouse use?
selections.notes: Useful for future material flow, but it will not replace a stacking mechanism on its own.
